projects.title: The Saltwater Clock
projects.description: A literary speculative novel set on a secluded North Atlantic island where tides dictate the passage of memory.

documents.title: Chapter 1: The Pendulum at Cape Vane
documents.content:
The lighthouse at Cape Vane had stood dark for seventeen years, but every equinox at dawn, the pendulum in its basement swung three inches wider.

Maren knelt by the brass escapement, grease staining the cuffs of her wool sweater. In the quiet damp beneath the granite floor, the Atlantic did not sound like waves; it sounded like breathing through clenched teeth. Her grandfather had left thirteen ledger volumes in the desk drawer upstairs, each page filled with tidal depth recordings and solitary numbers: 04:12, 11:47, 19:03.

"The sea does not measure minutes," he used to tell her, tapping the bronze face of the tide clock. "It measures what has been washed away and what is stubbornly left behind."

She stood up and wiped her palms on her apron. Outside, the gulls banked low against the slate-gray sky, their cries cut short by the rising wind. On the horizon, where nothing should have been anchored, a thin sliver of mast trembled between the breakers.

documents.title: Chapter 2: Calder’s Slipway
documents.content:
By noon, the harbor at Low Water was thick with mist.

Old Calder was mending cod nets on the slipway, his fingers warped like dried kelp. When Maren approached, he did not look up, but the rhythm of his netting needle paused.

"You were down in the lantern room again," Calder said. It was not a question.
"The escapement is slipping, Calder. The brass teeth are wearing down against the counterweight."
"Let it wear," he muttered. "Some gears are better left stopped."

Maren held out the scrap of parchment she had found slipped beneath the grandfather clock's plinth: a diagram of an offshore shoal that did not appear on any admiralty chart of the archipelago. Marked at the center was a solitary phrase in her grandfather's tight hand: 'Where the seventh bell drowns.'

story_contexts.synopsis: Maren inherits her estranged grandfather’s tidal lighthouse on Cape Vane and discovers its astronomical clock is tied to periodic oceanic memory anomalies. When an unregistered vessel appears in the dead zone, she must decipher his ledgers before the winter solstice tide.
story_contexts.characters:
Maren: Clockmaker and cartographer, cautious, driven by unresolved grief.
Calder: Island harbor elder, keeper of unwritten town taboos.
Elias: The missing grandfather whose ledgers contain unrecorded dates.
story_contexts.tone: Lyrical, quiet suspense, maritime atmosphere, philosophical.
story_contexts.active_question: Why did the grandfather deliberately alter the lighthouse escapement 17 years ago, and who is signaling from the shoal?

notes.title: Clockwork Mechanism Notes
notes.content: Deadbeat escapement with Graham pallets. Uses mercurial compensation pendulum to counteract salt-air thermal expansion. Weight-driven with a 30-day drop.

notes.title: General Craft: Pacing in Atmospheric Fiction
notes.content: Ground internal monologue in tactile physical objects (brass grease, brine-soaked wool, clock ticking). Let sensory details reveal character motivation.

ideas.title: The Submerged Bell Tower
ideas.content: The shoal on the grandfather’s chart is actually the summit of a submerged 17th-century parish church steeple that only surfaces during the extreme low spring tides of the solstice.

ideas.title: Calder’s True Allegiance
ideas.content: Calder was the apprentice who helped build the clock in 1968, but made a pact with the town council to silence it when the sound began driving the livestock mad.

ideas.title: The Price of Her Silence
ideas.content:
An external antagonist arrives, revealing that Elaina is currently acting as a double agent under duress, holding a secret that could destroy Dearil’s reputation. Dearil must now decide whether to protect her at the cost of his own moral integrity or expose her to save his future.

[Rationale: Creates a profound ethical dilemma that tests Dearil's capacity for sacrifice and forces a critical decision in the trajectory of the plot.]
